title: Second man dies in Surrey RCMP custody
article: The name of the second man to die in Surrey RCMP custody in less than two weeks was released by police yesterday, although they disclosed few details about the physical confrontation between the man and officers.
Ryan Wagemans, 24, of Langley, died in hospital Tuesday afternoon.
On Friday, Mr. Wagemans boarded a bus near 72nd Avenue and King George Highway in Surrey.
According to an RCMP media release, a Coast Mountain bus driver noticed Mr. Wagemans "exhibiting erratic behaviour" and contacted transit authorities.
Two unarmed security guards arrived and persuaded Mr. Wagemans to leave the bus. After he got off a scuffle ensued between Mr. Wagemans and the guards.
Surrey RCMP arrived to assist transit officials in securing Mr. Wagemans. He then "went into medical distress" and was taken to hospital where he died.
An autopsy was conducted yesterday, but the results won't be released for three months. No weapons were deployed during the incident.

The integrated homicide investigative team is reviewing the case. Spokesman Corporal Dale Carr said until investigators know definitively what caused the fight, or fights, details about the incident will not be released.
Coast Mountain Bus Co. is an operating subsidiary of TransLink. Ken Hardie, a TransLink spokesman, declined to comment on the incident.
Mr. Wagemans's death is the second in-custody fatality recently for Surrey RCMP.
On June 19, 46-year-old David Stitt died in hospital after he was involved in a scuffle with an RCMP officer and two passersby who came to her aid.
Mr. Stitt collapsed as he was being escorted into a police cruiser and died the following day.
